title: Compound Exercises
meta_desc: Discover the 5 compound exercises every NZ gym member should do, including squats, deadlifts and bench press, to improve overall fitness and strength, with tips on technique and beginner alternatives, and how to access affordable gym memberships through Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme.
intro: As a gym member in New Zealand, incorporating compound exercises into your workout routine is essential for building strength and improving overall fitness. Compound exercises work multiple muscle groups at once, making them a time-efficient and effective way to achieve your fitness goals. In this guide, we will cover the 5 compound exercises every NZ gym member should do, including tips on technique and beginner alternatives.

sections.heading: What are Compound Exercises?
sections.body: Compound exercises are multi-joint movements that work several muscle groups simultaneously. They are the most effective way to build strength, increase muscle mass, and improve overall fitness. Examples of compound exercises include squats, deadlifts, bench press, rows, and overhead press. These exercises are essential for any workout routine, regardless of your fitness level or goals.
list: Squats: work legs, glutes, and core
Deadlifts: work legs, back, and core
Bench press: work chest, shoulders, and triceps
Overhead press: work shoulders and triceps

sections.heading: Technique Tips for Compound Exercises
sections.body: Proper technique is crucial when performing compound exercises to avoid injury and get the most out of your workout. Here are some tips to keep in mind: start with a weight that allows you to maintain proper form, focus on slow and controlled movements, and engage your core throughout the exercise. It's also essential to warm up before starting your workout and to cool down afterwards to prevent injury.
list: Start with a weight that allows you to maintain proper form
Focus on slow and controlled movements
Engage your core throughout the exercise

sections.heading: Beginner Alternatives to Compound Exercises
sections.body: If you're new to weightlifting or find compound exercises too challenging, there are beginner-friendly alternatives you can start with. For example, instead of squats, you can start with bodyweight squats or use a leg press machine. Similarly, instead of deadlifts, you can start with a rowing machine or use lighter weights. Many NZ gyms, such as City Fitness and Les Mills, offer beginner-friendly equipment and classes that can help you get started with compound exercises.
list: Bodyweight squats instead of weighted squats
Leg press machine instead of squats

sections.heading: Accessing Affordable Gym Memberships
sections.body: Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme offers 40-70% off gym memberships at participating gyms, including Jetts and Anytime Fitness. This scheme is a great way to access affordable gym memberships and start your fitness journey. Many NZ gyms also offer free trials or guest passes, which can give you a taste of their facilities and classes before committing to a membership.
list: Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme: 40-70% off gym memberships
Free trials or guest passes at participating gyms

sections.heading: Get Started with Compound Exercises
sections.body: Now that you know the benefits of compound exercises and how to get started, it's time to take action. Compare gym memberships and find a gym that suits your needs and budget. Remember to start slow, focus on proper technique, and gradually increase the intensity of your workouts. With consistency and dedication, you can achieve your fitness goals and improve your overall health and wellbeing.
